facts.content: Patient has a sore throat followed by a dry cough lasting about one week.

facts.content: Patient has been off work for 3–4 days.

facts.source_text: SOB x 3–4 d (on exertion; able to walk/exercise)

facts.content: Patient experiences wheezing and mild chest pain.
Fever lasted for about 3 days and has now resolved.
Patient has intermittent headaches.

Patient denies having sputum, hemoptysis, nasal congestion, or rashes.
facts.source_text: Denies sputum, hemoptysis, nasal congestion, rashes

facts.content: Patient denies past medical history, including asthma and VTE.

facts.content: Patient is not currently on any medications.

facts.source_text: Non-smoker (rare experimentation); no known asbestos exposure

facts.content: Patient was born in the US and has lived in the UK for 12 years.
facts.source_text: born US, in UK x12 yrs

facts.content: Patient's recent travel was only to Europe.
Diagnosis of acute viral upper respiratory tract infection with dry cough and mild exertional SOB/wheeze.
facts.source_text: Acute viral URTI with dry cough; mild exertional SOB/wheeze; initial fever resolved; fluctuating but not progressive

facts.content: Work absence requires a sick note.
Decreased appetite during illness without weight loss.
Health anxiety regarding tuberculosis (TB) or cancer.
Paracetamol prescribed as needed, along with fluids and rest.
Safety-netting advice given to seek in-person GP review if condition worsens or changes suddenly.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: seek in-person GP review if SOB worsens/sudden change, new CP, or not improving over next 4–5 d; earlier if concerned

facts.content: Reassurance has been provided, with the explanation that tuberculosis or cancer is unlikely if symptoms resolve.
facts.source_text: Reassurance given; TB/Ca unlikely if symptoms resolve

facts.content: A sick note will be provided for a few more days off work.

facts.content: Monitor food intake and expect improvement in appetite as illness resolves.
